quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake. It can cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to make the motorcycle more stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake. It can cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can make the bike tip over. Use only the rear brake to slow down during the turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has a white background with red and black markings. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. It is yellow with black markings. It warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then apply it again quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will stay under control if it is straight and upright.

questions.question: You should keep a longer following distance:

options.text: When the pavement is slippery.
When traffic is light.
When you can see through vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Keep a longer following distance when your bike needs more time to stop. This includes slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy. Use at least a four-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, the minimum following distance is:

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep a minimum two-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as the dog approaches, then speed up quickly to get away.
Swerve around the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as the dog approaches, then speed up quickly to get away.
questions.explanation: When a dog approaches, slow down and shift to a lower gear. Once the dog gets close, speed up quickly to escape.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Ride close to the vehicle ahead so you can use its lights to see better.
Keep your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Slow down and stay farther behind the vehicle ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers.

questions.question: In general, what is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Good riders change their position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Stop completely and wait for a green arrow that points in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handgrips firmly and do not brake.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly and do not brake.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, grip the handlebars firmly and stay in a straight line. Only brake if you are sure which tire is flat. Slow down and leave the road safely.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from flat mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give you a wider view of the road than flat mirrors. However, they make cars coming toward you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Stay closer to the vehicle in front of you.
Stay farther from the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther from the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, increase your following distance. Slow down and adjust your position in the lane as needed.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the very front leading the group.
Near the front, right after the leader.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front, right after the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can guide them and watch them at the same time.

questions.question: When riding over rough pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to see the road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over rough pavement in a work zone. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: During the day when it is bright.
At dusk.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the day when it is bright.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even during daylight.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the middle of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic. This keeps you away from dangers like opening car doors and people stepping between parked cars. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the middle of your lane to give yourself more space.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn about your specific motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, where should it be placed?

options.text: Over the rear axle.
On the gas tank in front of you.
Piled against the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on their motorcycle.

questions.question: What usually causes a wobble (sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars)?

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven load.
The front wheel is not fastened tightly to the frame.
The front tire hit an object.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven load.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake from side to side. It is usually caused by improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.
No, but it is recommended.
Yes, only for new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection when riding a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a railroad crossing.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcycles pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcycles should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one starts.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, do one action first, then do the other.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. This is the safest position. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too early.
